req.title: Delete unknown returns 404
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 404 when DELETE targets a non-existent task id.

doc.reasoning: R-TASK-014 requires HTTP 404 when DELETE targets a non-existent task id. Six test cases are designed: (1) positive/EP — DELETE an existing task id returns 204, confirming the happy path; (2) negative/NEG — DELETE a clearly non-existent id returns exactly 404 with the correct detail message; (3) boundary/BVA — DELETE id=21 (one above the highest pre-loaded id=20) returns 404, catching off-by-one mutations; (4) boundary/BVA — DELETE id=20 (highest pre-loaded id) returns 204, confirming no spurious 404 at upper boundary; (5) negative/DT — state-transition test: first DELETE removes task, second DELETE returns 404 (catches mutations that skip existence check); heuristic changed from STC to DT because STC is reserved for positive state-transition coverage and this test exercises a negative outcome after a state change, fitting the decision-table row 'task absent => 404'; (6) negative/NEG — full response structure validation for 404 body.

tests.name: test_delete_existing_task_returns_204
preconditions: Task with id=1 exists in the pre-loaded dataset
trace: R-TASK-014: confirms 404 is NOT returned for an existing task (EP — valid partition)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)
r = client.delete("/tasks/1")
assert r.status_code == 204
assert r.content == b""

tests.name: test_delete_nonexistent_task_returns_404
preconditions: Task with id=99999 does not exist in the database
expected: Response JSON detail contains 'Task with id 99999 not found'
trace: R-TASK-014: system shall respond with HTTP 404 when DELETE targets a non-existent task id
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)
r = client.delete("/tasks/99999")
assert r.status_code == 404
body = r.json()
assert body["detail"] == "Task with id 99999 not found"

tests.name: test_delete_max_preloaded_id_returns_204_not_404
preconditions: Task with id=20 exists in the pre-loaded dataset (boundary: highest pre-loaded id)
expected: HTTP 204 No Content — id=20 exists so 404 must NOT be returned
trace: R-TASK-014: BVA at upper boundary of pre-loaded ids; confirms 404 is not spuriously raised for the last valid id — catches off-by-one mutations

tests.name: test_delete_already_deleted_task_returns_404
preconditions: Task with id=2 exists in the pre-loaded dataset
First DELETE removes the task successfully
actions: Send DELETE /tasks/2 (second call — task no longer exists)
expected: Second DELETE returns HTTP 404 with detail 'Task with id 2 not found'
trace: R-TASK-014: DT — decision table row: task transitions from 'exists' to 'deleted'; second delete must return 404 (catches mutations that skip the existence check after deletion)
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)
r1 = client.delete("/tasks/2")
assert r1.status_code == 204
assert r1.content == b""
r2 = client.delete("/tasks/2")
assert r2.status_code == 404
body = r2.json()
assert body["detail"] == "Task with id 2 not found"

tests.name: test_delete_nonexistent_task_response_structure
preconditions: Task with id=55555 does not exist
expected: detail value is exactly 'Task with id 55555 not found'
trace: R-TASK-014: NEG — task absent => 404 with structured error body; catches mutations on status code constant (404->400, 404->200) and detail string
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)
r = client.delete("/tasks/55555")
assert r.status_code == 404
body = r.json()
assert "detail" in body
assert body["detail"] == "Task with id 55555 not found"
assert r.headers["content-type"].startswith("application/json")
